html:
A vaccine against Covid 19 made by BioNTech, a German biotech company in Mainz, with the American firm Pfizer running trials and production. On 2 December 2020 Britain approved it, the first Covid vaccine approved anywhere after full clinical trials.

BioNTech was founded by the doctors Uğur Şahin and Özlem Türeci, a married couple both of Turkish origin, to fight cancer with messenger RNA. The vaccine gives the body a short genetic message to make the virus's spike protein, so the immune system learns to recognise it. Work by Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman made such RNA safe to inject; they won the Nobel Prize in 2023.

Design began in January 2020, within days of the virus's genetic code being published, and approval came less than a year later, far faster than any vaccine before. Billions of doses were given during the COVID-19 pandemic.
